newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity down sharply as natgas tumbles.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity down sharply as natgas tumbles.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures, especially the January and February contracts, were down sharply in early trade amid warmer weather and lower natural gas prices, market sources said Monday.
"It is all related to the weather. Natgas is off and so is electricity," said one dealer.
Traders also cited lower price offers from Bonneville Power Administration in the Northwest, where hydroelectric supplies are expected to be ample, as putting downward pressure on cash electricity.
In addition, the restart over the weekend of a 755 megawatt (MW) unit at the Navajo coal-fired generating plan in Arizona has added to the regional supply picture, they said.

January 1997 California-Oregon border (COB) futures were down $3.10 at $23.25 per megawatt hour (MWh) as of 1245 EST, while the February contract was down $2.00 at $17.75. Other active COB contracts were down 10 to 65 cents.
January Palo Verde was down $2.93 at $24.60 per MWh, while February was down 20 cents at $21.75. Other PV contracts were down 20 to 35 cents.
As of 1210 EST, 70 COB and 50 PV contracts were sold.
